definition.def: If you devote yourself, your time, or your energy to something, you spend all or most of your time or energy on it.
examples: He decided to devote the rest of his life to scientific investigation. [VERB noun + to]
Considerable resources have been devoted to proving him a liar. [VERB noun + to]
She gladly gave up her part-time job to devote herself entirely to her art. [VERB pronoun-reflexive + to]

definition.def: If you devote a particular proportion of a piece of writing or a speech to a particular subject, you deal with the subject in that amount of space or time.
examples: He devoted a major section of his massive report to an analysis of U.S. aircraft design. [VERB noun + to]
In her 900-page memoirs, only four pages are devoted to the arts. [VERB noun to noun]

examples.sentence: This seems an extremely optimistic proposition from a man who must be aware of the failings and weaknesses of the zoo industry the man who, when a member of the council of London Zoo, had to persuade the zoo to devote more of its activities to conservation.
